summary.text: Adrian Maher is running as an independent for Mornington at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in Mount Eliza and went to school locally, and his campaign site says he has spent over 30 years running large programs and transformation projects in industry. He has pledged to withhold confidence, supply and support for legislation from any government that does not commit to fully funding one of his listed local promises, and he has asked residents not to donate to his campaign.

sources.title: Mornington: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Ashli Beards is One Nation's candidate for Mornington at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from Watsonia North in Melbourne's north, she moved to the Mornington Peninsula about 14 years ago, according to the ABC. Her legal practice has taken in criminal as well as corporate and commercial work.

sources.title: Mornington: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Chris Crewther has been the Liberal member for Mornington since 2022, having won preselection over the sitting member David Morris. He was previously the federal member for Dunkley from 2016 until his defeat in 2019. He has been the Liberal whip in the Assembly since 2022 and stood for the party leadership in December 2024. He is recontesting Mornington in 2026.

summary.text: Gene Brownlie is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Mornington at the 2026 Victorian election. On the party's site he says he came to the area to help look after an older relative, and that he has done community organising for over ten years. The ABC had not published a biography of him as at early November 2026.

Outside study and work he volunteers as a paralegal and helps run community events.

summary.text: Kerry Macdonald is Labor's candidate for Mornington, a marginal Liberal seat, at the 2026 Victorian election. A Mount Martha local, she started out teaching in secondary schools, then held senior public service posts in health, human services and treasury for two decades before moving into management consulting. She is president of Labor's Mornington branch and belongs to the Labor Environment Action Network.

summary.text: Melissa Goffin is an independent candidate for Mornington at the 2026 Victorian election. After about ten years as a teacher in public schools she went into business, and she is managing director of Red Gum BBQ, a restaurant business on the Peninsula. She chairs Women in Business Mornington Peninsula & Frankston, helped found and organise the Melbourne Women's March, and has sat on small business boards and a NAB customer advisory board.
